## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical control of data exfiltration in a multi‑account AWS setup, focusing on real‑world patterns: IAM drift, bucket policies, data discovery, and incident response.

## Key Concepts
- Least privilege and permission boundaries
- Cross‑account access controls and SCPs
- Data discovery and DLP tooling (Macie, CloudTrail logs)
- Incident response runbooks and SLAs

## Detection (0–4h)
- Enable CloudTrail with Lake integration for centralized logging
- Deploy Macie to discover and classify sensitive billing data
- Create EventBridge rules for s3:GetObject on the billing bucket from untrusted principals

## Containment (4–12h)
- Revoke the legacy IAM role immediately
- Rotate any credentials that may have been exposed
- Temporarily restrict cross‑account access until remediation is complete

## Recovery (12–24h)
- Apply an IAM SCP to limit cross‑account permissions
- Update bucket policies to deny GetObject unless the principal is in the trusted account
- Disable bucket public access

## Post‑Incident (24–48h)
- Deploy AWS Config rules to detect unauthorized IAM changes
- Implement automated remediation via EventBridge and Lambda
- Conduct a post‑mortem and document lessons learned

## Success Criteria
- No unauthorized access to billing data within 48 hours
- All cross‑account access follows least privilege
- Automated detection and remediation operational

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical supply chain security knowledge at a beginner level, focusing on concrete tooling (cosign, Sigstore), per-tenant isolation, and IR readiness.

## Key Concepts
- Image signing and provenance with cosign/Sigstore
- Per-tenant registries and image provenance policies
- CI secret scanning and SBOM generation
- Short-lived credentials for runners and secure secret handling
- 48-hour incident response playbook with runbooks and dashboards

## Code Example
```yaml
name: Verify image provenance
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
jobs:
  verify-image:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up cosign
        run: |
          curl -sSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sigstore/cosign/v1.6.0/cosign-linux-amd64 -o cosign
          chmod +x cosign
      - name: Verify image provenance
        run: |
          ./cosign verify ghcr.io/tenant/registry/service:latest --certificate cosign.pub
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you roll this out to 100 tenants with minimal ops? 
- What metrics and dashboards would you use to detect tampering early?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked
This evaluates understanding of data isolation in shared ML infrastructure, origin-bound access tokens, rapid incident response for cross-tenant data leakage, and practical tooling decisions for enterprise-grade security.

## Key Concepts
- Tenant isolation in feature stores and vector databases
- Fine-grained IAM with attribute-based access control (ABAC)
- API gateway runtime validation using policy engines (OPA/Rego)
- Envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS keys
- Audit trails, data lineage, and compliance logging
- Incident response playbook with containment, eradication, and recovery phases

## Code Example
```rego
package policy.tenant_isolation

default allow = false

allow {
    input.tenant == data.tenants[input.tenant_id].owner
    input.action == "read"
    input.resource_namespace == input.tenant_id
    not exceeds_quota(input.tenant_id, input.request_size)
}

allow {
    input.tenant == data.tenants[input.tenant_id].owner
    input.action == "write"
    input.resource_namespace == input.tenant_id
    input.token_expires_at > time.now_ns()
}

exceeds_quota(tenant_id, size) {
    data.tenants[tenant_id].quota_used + size > data.tenants[tenant_id].quota_limit
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate tenant boundaries without introducing significant latency at inference time?
- What monitoring alerts would trigger automatic containment actions?
- How do you handle key rotation for envelope encryption without downtime?
